shortTitle: Critical View of the Myopectineal Orifice (CV-MPO)
title: Critical View of the Myopectineal Orifice
citation: Daes J, Felix E. Ann Surg. 2017;266(1):e1-e2.
learningObjectives: State what ‘Critical View of the MPO’ means in one sentence.
Judge whether a given dissection meets CV-MPO (Yes/No).
Identify which component is missing when CV-MPO is not achieved.
paperIn3MinBullets: Defines a ‘critical view’ endpoint for MIS inguinal hernia repair analogous to the critical view concept in cholecystectomy.
Emphasizes standardization and a binary safety checkpoint before mesh placement.
The goal is not nuance; the goal is a minimum exposure standard.
Pairs well with Inverted Y / Five Triangles as an orientation tool to achieve the endpoint.

activities.title: CV-MPO reference image
activities.instructions: This is the ‘complete’ reference. Everything else is judged against this.

activities.title: Is CV-MPO achieved?
activities.prompt: Is the critical view achieved in this image?
activities.explanation: If no, identify the missing exposure elements.

activities.title: What is missing?
activities.prompt: Which element is missing for CV-MPO?
choices: Lateral space opened for mesh wing
activities.explanation: Use the paper’s definition of the endpoint; if any required element is absent, answer ‘No’.

flashcards.back: A minimum anatomic exposure standard in MIS inguinal repair that must be achieved before mesh placement to ensure full coverage and avoid complications.

flashcards.front: If CV-MPO is not achieved, the right action is:
flashcards.back: Continue dissection until required anatomic exposure is obtained; do not ‘settle’ and place mesh early.

choices: A binary endpoint defining minimum exposure before mesh placement

quiz.q: The most appropriate use of CV-MPO is:
If CV-MPO is not achieved, you should:
choices: Continue dissection to meet exposure standard
